## CEO BRIEFING

Dana — state of play ahead of your 15:00 board call. All times UTC; the incident is still live at 14:20.

**What happened**
A Batch API incident began at 11:42 today: elevated 502 errors on `POST /v1/batch/jobs`. It was confined to one of our two Batch worker fleets. Other Northstar API surfaces (Inference, Embeddings, Files) are unaffected. At 12:58 we applied a mitigation — moving all Batch API traffic to the healthy fleet — and the error rate fell immediately. We are in the post-mitigation verification period; the incident is not yet resolved.

**Who is hit**
- 17,602 of 58,900 Batch API requests failed during the 11:42–12:58 window — about **29.9%**. This is the headline impact figure.
- Seven Batch API accounts were affected: Stark Industries, Contoso, Wayne Enterprises, Globex, Wonka Industries, Umbrella Health and Initech. All sat on the affected worker fleet. Two other Batch API accounts had no failures.
- The Batch API is a small share of overall volume — roughly 7% of the 842,000 requests served platform-wide in the window.
- Contoso is the only affected account whose contract carries service credits.

**Where we are**
Mitigated and recovering, not resolved. Error rate is ~0.3% against a 0.2% baseline. Our verification window closes at 14:30; policy requires 90 minutes of continuous normal error rate before we can call it resolved. Root cause is not established.

**What you can say if it comes up**
- There was an incident affecting the Batch API, starting at 11:42; a mitigation has been applied and the service is recovering; we are monitoring before confirming recovery; a further update will follow.
- Please don't describe it as resolved, fixed or closed — verification has not finished and the cause is not confirmed.
- If asked about cause, say it remains under investigation. Note that a 12:05 public status update used the word "identified" and referred to a fix; that was premature — the cause has not been established.
- On credits: we cannot yet say whether November will breach the 99.9% commitment. Monthly availability is measured across the covered services for the calendar month and is determined after month end, published within 10 business days. Contoso has asked; our reply does not confirm a breach or a credit.

## ENGINEERING UPDATE

INC-2026-1109-01 — handover at 14:20 UTC. **Status: OPEN** (mitigated; verification in progress; root cause not established).

**What happened**
- **11:31** — `batch-api@2026.11.09-r3` rolled out to both fleets. Small changeset; includes max DB pool size lowered 80 → 24 per worker.
- **11:38** — fleet-a submission volume climbs; ~3x the morning average by 11:50, driven by a large scheduled job from wonka-industries.
- **11:42** — first page: `batch_api_5xx_rate` over threshold on fleet-a; 502s on `POST /v1/batch/jobs`. Incident start.
- **11:44** — errors confined to fleet-a; fleet-b clean. Not the gateway, not the SDK.
- **11:47** — upstream object-storage provider ruled out (provider status green; Files API healthy on the same provider).
- **12:03** — fleet-a workers queueing on DB connections; correlation to the r3 pool change noted, **not tested**.
- **12:31** — decision: no r3 rollback yet (would destroy the evidence); move traffic instead.
- **12:58** — mitigation: all Batch traffic cut to fleet-b; fleet-a drained and held out of rotation. Error rate fell to 0.4% within two minutes.

**Where we are now**
- Error rate ~0.3% (baseline 0.2%). fleet-b queue depth normal. No new customer failures since cutover.
- Verification window open until **14:30** (10 minutes from now); policy requires 90 minutes of continuous normal error rate — nothing can be called resolved before 14:30.
- Re-drive of failed jobs ~60% complete across affected accounts, with no failures on re-drive.
- fleet-a remains out of rotation.

**Open items / next**
- Root cause not established. **H1** (pool change in r3) is leading; **H2** (concentrated load on fleet-a) is still live; they may interact. Both untested. **H3** (upstream provider) rejected. The r3 rollback test has not been run.
- Finish the re-drive.
- After the window closes clean at 14:30: confirm recovery, then decide on returning fleet-a to rotation and on running the rollback test.
- Marcus's internal planning estimate is wrap-up and fleet-a back in rotation around 16:00 — **internal only, not for external use.**

**Owners:** Priya — on call; executed cutover; running the re-drive. Marcus — leading the root-cause investigation. Ruth — public status page. Tomas — support/customer comms.

## CUSTOMER EMAIL

To: Contoso
Subject: Re: Batch API tickets TKT-8903 / TKT-8907 — incident and Schedule B

Hello,

Thank you for flagging this, and apologies for the disruption.

**What happened and your impact**
An incident affecting the Batch API began at 11:42 UTC today and was mitigated at 12:58 UTC. During the affected window (11:42–12:58 UTC), your account's Batch API traffic was as follows:

- Batch API requests: 9,400
- Failed requests (502): 3,410
- First failure: 11:43 UTC; last failure: 12:56 UTC

That is approximately 36% of your Batch API requests in the window.

**Current status**
A mitigation has been applied and the service is recovering. We are monitoring before we confirm recovery, and we will send you a further update by 15:00 UTC.

**On Schedule B (service credits)**
We are not able to confirm at this point whether November will breach the 99.9% commitment, or what credit would apply. Under Schedule B, Monthly Availability is calculated across the Covered Services for the calendar month and is determined by Northstar from its service records after month end, published within 10 business days of month end; any credit claim is then submitted within 30 days of that publication (B.5). We will publish the November figure in line with that process.

We will keep this ticket updated.

Regards,
Northstar Support — Incident Command

## STATUS PAGE UPDATE

**2026-11-09 14:20 — Batch API incident: mitigation applied, monitoring**

We continue to work on the incident affecting the Batch API that began at 11:42 UTC. A mitigation has been applied and the service is recovering. We are monitoring before we confirm recovery. We will post our next update by 15:00 UTC.

*Monitoring.*
